text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.45% today to $457.22, continuing a five-day slide that has wiped out 4.4% since mid-October. The decline comes despite crude oil prices hitting six-month highs—Brent crude topped $116 today—driven by escalating Middle East tensions and U.S. threats of military action against Iran. For a refiner like Marathon, higher crude costs are a headwind: refiners buy oil at spot prices and sell refined products (gasoline, diesel) at prices that don't always move in lockstep, so rising crude can compress profit margins in the short term.

The broader energy trade is benefiting U.S. exporters of liquefied natural gas and other sellers who profit from geopolitical supply fears, but refiners face a squeeze when crude rallies faster than their output can be priced. With refineries running at 93.4% capacity and storage levels moderate, Marathon is locked into high feedstock costs without the immediate pricing power to pass that on—a classic refiner dilemma in a spiking crude environment.
